text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc Thursday said its board elected James Zimmerman as chairman and chief executive, succeeding Allen Questrom, who is leaving in May after a 30-year career with Federated.
Zimmerman, 52, has served as Federated's president and chief operating officer since May 1988.

The retailer also said that Terry Lundgren has been named president and chief merchandising officer of Federated. Lundgren, 44, has been chairman of the company's New York-based Federated Merchandising and Product Development division since February 1994.
The transition to the new Zimmerman/Lundgren management partnership will be effective with the close of business at Federated's May 16, 1997 annual shareholders' meeting.
At that meeting, Lundgren also will stand for shareholder election to the company's board of directors.

Questrom, 57, has served as chairman/CEO of Federated since February 1990. Although his current contract with the company expires in February 1998, Questrom said he has accomplished his goals -- helping to bring the company out of bankruptcy, overseeing the acquisitions and successful integration of both Macy's and Broadway Stores into Federated, restoring the company's leadership position in retailing and putting in place a strong succession team.
"Having done what I set out to do, the time now is right for me to leave," Questrom said in a statement.
Federated said both Zimmerman and Lundgren have worked for the company for many years which will allow for management continuity and a seamless transition.
In 1994, Questrom successfully led the company's acquisitions of R. H. Macy & Co. Inc. and Broadway Stores Inc.

Federated is the nation's largest department store retailer with annual sales of more than $15 billion. Federated currently operates more than 400 department stores and 150 specialty stores in 36 states. Federated's department stores operate nationally under the names of Bloomingdale's, The Bon Marche, Burdines, Goldsmith's, Lazarus, Macy's, Rich's and Stern's.
